appraisal_cycles.label: Apr 5 – Apr 19, 2026
appraisal_cycles.assessment: Strongest cycle yet for depth over breadth. KYC Phase 1 shipped with 11/11 tests passing — first real document upload and verification flow across any product in the portfolio. Security audit produced a full cross-project risk matrix with a NOW/IMMEDIATE/LATER fix plan. Wrap automation is genuinely integrated. Graphs moved to a dedicated tab on both desktop and mobile. Consistent gaps: auth permanently deferred (FEAT-036 is now 4 cycles untouched — this is no longer a gap, it is a decision to not ship. The next cycle must treat it as non-negotiable), mobile-first still reactive (mobile added after desktop, not before), prompt batching improving but not closed. Critical unlock heading into next cycle: Supabase storage bucket config + Render env vars for KYC doc upload — that’s the last mile on ARIA KYC Phase 1. Auth must ship on one product. Four cycles of deferral is a pattern, not a plan.

appraisal_cycles.label: Mar 21 – Apr 5, 2026
appraisal_cycles.assessment: Product-minded builder who moves fast and ships real products. Systems thinking is now proven — memory, triggers, wrap protocol, and command centre are live infrastructure that compounds. Strategic clarity strong: knows what to solve and what to park. Consistent gaps: auth permanently deferred (FEAT-036 is now 3+ cycles untouched — the single biggest unlock unshipped), passive receiving (improving but not closed — still accepts Claude output without challenging tradeoffs), mobile-first not yet reflexive (rule exists, practice lags), prompt batching (serial UI fixes still trigger repeat deploys). Biggest unlock this cycle: wrap automation is genuinely wired in (wrap_update.py + session_wrap.md + validation gate). That's infrastructure actually running, not just documented. The question heading into the next cycle: does the same systems discipline get applied to auth and production-grade security?
